meta.titre: Fats and Oils in Cookery: Functions, Effects of Heat, Deep Frying and Air in Mixtures
meta.sous_theme: Functions of fats, effects of heat, deep frying rules and mechanical raising methods

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: In a Yaounde snack stall, plantain chips are dropped into hot oil and come out golden in minutes, while next door a baker rubs margarine into flour for rock cakes. Fats and oils do many jobs in the kitchen, and they can also cause burns, fires and bad flavours if they are mishandled. The GCE asks about the rules of deep frying, the effects of heat on fats and the ways in which air is beaten into mixtures, so you need to give each answer in the exact number of points asked.

items: Fats and oils are nutrients that supply energy and carry some vitamins.
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius and fats can be heated far above this temperature.
Air expands when heated, and steam is formed when water is heated enough.

sections.titre: Fats and oils: functions, effects of heat and safe frying
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Fats and oils
Fats are solid at room temperature and oils are liquid. Both come from animals or plants.

| Source | Examples |
|---|---|
| Animal | butter, lard, suet, dripping, fish oils |
| Plant | red palm oil, groundnut oil, sunflower oil, soya oil; margarine is made mostly from vegetable oils |

### Functions in cookery
1. Shortening: fat coats flour particles, so pastry and biscuits are crumbly and tender.
2. Aeration: creaming fat with sugar traps air which makes cakes rise.
3. Frying: oil can be made much hotter than boiling water, so food cooks quickly and browns.
4. Flavour and richness: fat adds taste and a smooth feel.
5. Moistness: cakes stay moist for longer.
6. Layering: fat rolled between layers of dough gives flaky pastry.
7. Emulsions: oil and egg yolk can be beaten into a thick sauce such as mayonnaise.

### Effects of heat on fats
| Stage | What happens |
|---|---|
| Gentle heat | solid fat softens and melts into oil |
| Stronger heat | the fat becomes much hotter than boiling water; food fries and browns |
| Smoking point | the fat begins to break down and gives off irritating blue smoke and a bad smell |
| Higher still | the vapour can catch fire |
| Repeated heating | the fat darkens, thickens and tastes stale, and breaks down more easily |
| Water added to hot fat | the fat spits and splashes dangerously |

Fat that is stored in a warm, light, airy place goes rancid, with an unpleasant smell and taste.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to outline rules, precautions or safety measures for deep frying.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give each rule with a reason. 1. Use a deep, heavy pan with a basket, filled not more than half full, so that the oil cannot boil over. 2. Use a suitable oil that does not smoke too easily, such as refined groundnut or vegetable oil. 3. Heat the oil to about 180 degrees Celsius: a small cube of bread should turn golden in about a minute. 4. Dry the food well or coat it, because wet food makes the oil spit. 5. Fry small batches and lower the food gently; too much food cools the oil and makes the food greasy. 6. Never leave the pan unattended. 7. Drain the fried food on absorbent paper. 8. When the oil is cool, strain it and keep it covered, and discard it when dark or smelly. 9. If the oil catches fire, switch off the heat and smother the flames with a lid or damp cloth; never throw water on it.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked how air is put into cakes, batters and pastry by physical action.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Mechanical methods add air by action: 1. Sieving flour puts air between the particles. 2. Creaming beats fat and sugar until pale and fluffy. 3. Whisking eggs or egg whites holds air in a foam. 4. Beating a batter brings in air. 5. Folding in flour with a metal spoon keeps the air. 6. Rubbing fat into flour traps a little air. 7. Rolling and folding pastry in layers traps air between the fat and dough. The trapped air expands in the oven and makes the mixture rise. Choose the exact number asked and say how each one adds air.

variantes.nom: Explaining the effects of heat on fats
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to explain briefly what happens when fat is heated.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Describe the stages in order: the fat melts, then becomes very hot, then reaches the smoking point and breaks down, and finally catches fire. Add that repeated heating darkens the fat, spoils the flavour and makes it less suitable to eat, and that water makes hot fat spit.

sections.enonce_markdown: A student is deep frying plantain chips at home. (a) State four rules she should follow. (b) What would happen to the chips if the oil were too cool? (c) She uses 2 litres of oil costing 1\,600 FCFA per litre (assumed price) and uses the same oil 5 times. Calculate the cost of the oil for each frying. (8 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command words and marks.
etapes.justification: 'State four rules' needs four separate rules; a short reason makes each one clear. Part (b) needs an effect and part (c) a calculation.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Four rules, one effect, one calculation.

etapes.justification: They must be different and be practical.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Use a deep pan filled less than half full; heat the oil to the right temperature; dry the food and fry small batches; never leave the pan unattended.

etapes.justification: Cool oil cannot seal the surface of the food quickly, so it soaks in.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The chips become pale, soft and greasy.

etapes.action: Find the total cost of the oil.
etapes.justification: Multiply the volume by the price per litre.

etapes.action: Divide by the number of uses.
etapes.justification: The same oil is used five times, so each frying takes one fifth of the cost.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **(a)** Use a deep, stable pan filled less than half full so that the oil cannot boil over; heat the oil to the right temperature and test it with a cube of bread; dry the food and fry small batches; never leave the pan unattended. **(b)** The chips would be pale, soft and greasy because they absorb the oil. **(c)** Total cost 3,200 FCFA; cost per frying **640 FCFA**.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing 'put water on a burning pan of oil' as a safety rule.
items.pourquoi_faux: Water sinks under the hot oil, turns to steam at once and throws burning oil upwards, spreading the fire.
items.correction_markdown: Switch off the heat and smother the flames with a lid or a damp cloth.

items.erreur_markdown: Listing only five rules when six were asked for.
items.pourquoi_faux: Each missing rule loses a mark, and a rule repeated in other words is counted once.
items.correction_markdown: Count the points before you finish and give one rule per line with a different idea.

items.erreur_markdown: Answering 'explain the effects of heat on fats' with only 'it melts'.
items.pourquoi_faux: Melting is only the first stage. The question expects the later stages too, and a one-word answer cannot earn full marks.
items.correction_markdown: Say that the fat melts, gets very hot, smokes and breaks down at the smoking point, and may then catch fire; add that repeated heating spoils it.

items.erreur_markdown: Calling folding or whisking a chemical method of raising a mixture.
items.pourquoi_faux: Whisking, creaming, sieving and folding put air in by physical action, so they are mechanical methods. Baking powder is the chemical method.
items.correction_markdown: Classify by how the gas is produced: physical action is mechanical, baking powder is chemical.

items.erreur_markdown: Filling the frying pan almost to the top with oil so that more chips can be fried at once.
items.pourquoi_faux: Hot oil bubbles up when food is added and can boil over onto the flame, causing burns or a fire.
items.correction_markdown: Fill the pan not more than half full and fry in small batches.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Name two animal fats and two vegetable oils. (b) State one function of fat in making pastry.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Animal fats: any two of **butter, lard, suet, dripping**. Vegetable oils: any two of **red palm oil, groundnut oil, sunflower oil, soya oil**. (b) It **shortens** the pastry: fat coats the flour particles, so the pastry is crumbly and tender (it also adds flavour).

items.enonce_markdown: A recipe uses 60 g of cooking fat to make 12 buns. Take fat as giving 37 kJ of energy per gram. (a) Calculate the mass of fat in one bun. (b) Calculate the energy from fat in one bun. (c) Calculate the energy from fat in three buns. (d) Name one health problem that can come from eating too much fat.
items.solution_markdown: (a) $60 \div 12 = 5$, so **5 g**. (b) $5 \times 37 = 185$, so **185 kJ**. (c) $3 \times 185 = 555$, so **555 kJ**. (d) **Obesity** (or heart disease).

items.enonce_markdown: A cook leaves a pan of oil on a high flame and answers a telephone call. When she returns, blue smoke is rising and the oil has turned dark. (a) Explain what is happening to the oil and what may happen next. (b) Describe the safe action to take. (c) Give two reasons why oil should not be reused many times. (7 marks)
items.solution_markdown: (a) The oil has passed its smoking point: it is breaking down and giving off irritating smoke, and the dark colour shows it is being spoilt. If heating continues, the vapour may catch fire. (b) **Switch off the heat**, cover the pan with its lid or a damp cloth to cut off air, leave it to cool, and never use water. (c) Any two: repeated heating darkens the oil and spoils its flavour; it breaks down more easily and smokes at a lower temperature; the food fried in it tastes stale; old, dark oil is less suitable to eat.

items_markdown: Fats are solid and oils are liquid at room temperature; they come from animals and plants.
Functions: shortening, aeration, frying, flavour, moistness, layering in pastry and emulsions such as mayonnaise.
Heat melts fat, then makes it very hot, then it smokes and breaks down, and finally it can catch fire; repeated heating spoils it, and water makes it spit.
Deep frying rules: a deep pan less than half full, correct temperature, dry food, small batches, never unattended, drain, strain and store the oil, and smother a fire without water.
Mechanical methods of raising: sieving, creaming, whisking, beating, folding, rubbing in, and rolling and folding.
